roleplays.title: Job Interview
roleplays.description: Practice a first-round interview for a product or operations role.
roleplays.workplaceContext: A hiring manager wants to understand your experience, motivation and communication style.
roleplays.userGoal: Give focused answers using situation, action and result.
roleplays.openingLine: Thanks for joining today. Could you start by telling me a little about yourself?

promptVariants.title: Tell me about yourself
promptVariants.openingLine: Thanks for joining today. Could you start by telling me a little about yourself?
promptVariants.userGoal: Give a concise career story with your role, strongest proof point and reason for applying.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Use present, past and future: who you are now, what experience proves it and why this role is next.

promptVariants.title: Why this role?
promptVariants.openingLine: What interests you most about this role and our company?
promptVariants.userGoal: Connect your motivation to the role, the company and your next professional step.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Avoid a generic answer. Mention one role requirement and one reason it fits your experience.

promptVariants.title: Difficult situation
promptVariants.openingLine: Can you describe a difficult work situation and how you handled it?
promptVariants.userGoal: Use situation, action and result with one clear lesson learned.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Keep the problem short, spend most of the answer on what you did and end with the result.

suggestedPhrases: In my previous role, I was responsible for...
followUpPrompts: That sounds useful. Can you give me one specific example of a result you created?
What would your previous manager say is your strongest communication skill?

feedback.summary: Your answer is professional and easy to follow. The next improvement is to add one specific result.
improvements: Close with why the role fits your next step
feedback.suggestedRewrite: In my previous role, I coordinated weekly customer feedback reviews. The main challenge was turning scattered notes into clear product priorities. I created a simple scoring system, and as a result, the team reduced follow-up time by about 20%.

roleplays.title: Meeting Practice
roleplays.description: Practice joining a weekly project meeting and giving a useful update.
roleplays.workplaceContext: Your team needs a short update on progress, blockers and next steps.
roleplays.userGoal: Explain what is done, what is blocked and what support you need.
roleplays.openingLine: Let's start with your update. What changed since our last meeting?

promptVariants.title: Status update
promptVariants.openingLine: Let's start with your update. What changed since our last meeting?
promptVariants.userGoal: Explain what is done, what is blocked and what support you need.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Use three short parts: progress, blocker and next step.

promptVariants.title: Clarify deadline
promptVariants.openingLine: The timeline looks tight. What deadline or dependency do you need clarified?
promptVariants.userGoal: Ask for one specific clarification without sounding defensive.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Name the dependency, explain the risk briefly and ask for a clear owner or date.

promptVariants.title: Challenge decision
promptVariants.openingLine: I think we should move forward with the current plan. Do you see any risks?
promptVariants.userGoal: Politely challenge the plan with one risk and one constructive alternative.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Start by acknowledging the plan, then add your concern and suggest a practical next step.

suggestedPhrases: Since our last meeting, I completed...
followUpPrompts: Thanks. What support do you need from the team before the next meeting?
If the blocker continues, what backup plan would you suggest?

feedback.summary: The update is clear, but it needs a sharper ask at the end.
feedback.suggestedRewrite: Since our last meeting, I finished the first draft and shared it with design. The main blocker is that I need final pricing details from finance. Could we confirm who owns that by tomorrow?

roleplays.title: Presentation Practice
roleplays.description: Practice a short presentation about a business idea or project update.
roleplays.workplaceContext: You are presenting a recommendation to a small leadership group.
roleplays.userGoal: Give a structured opening and transition smoothly between points.
roleplays.openingLine: Before you begin, what should we pay attention to during your presentation?

promptVariants.title: Opening agenda
promptVariants.openingLine: Before you begin, what should we pay attention to during your presentation?
promptVariants.userGoal: Open with the topic, the three-part structure and the decision you want from the audience.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Start with the purpose, preview the structure and tell the audience what decision or takeaway matters.

promptVariants.title: Smooth transition
promptVariants.openingLine: You finished your first point. How would you move naturally into the second point?
promptVariants.userGoal: Use a clear transition that connects the previous point to the next business reason.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Avoid saying only 'next'. Link the ideas with a phrase like 'This matters because...' or 'That leads to...'.

promptVariants.title: Handle challenge
promptVariants.openingLine: I understand the recommendation, but why should we prioritize this now?
promptVariants.userGoal: Answer a skeptical question with calm reasoning, evidence and one practical next step.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Acknowledge the concern first, then give one reason, one proof point and a small next step.

suggestedPhrases: Today I will cover three points...
This leads to the second point...
followUpPrompts: What is the one decision you want the audience to make after your presentation?
How would you answer if someone challenges your recommendation?

feedback.summary: The presentation has a strong opening. Add clearer signposting before each main point.
feedback.suggestedRewrite: Today I will cover the customer problem, the proposed solution and the next decision we need. The key takeaway is that we can test this with a small pilot before making a larger investment.

roleplays.title: Sales Call
roleplays.description: Practice a consultative sales conversation with a potential customer.
roleplays.workplaceContext: A prospect is interested but unsure whether the solution is worth the cost.
roleplays.userGoal: Ask about business pain, confirm value and respond calmly to price concerns.
roleplays.openingLine: I understand what your product does, but I'm not sure the price makes sense for us.

promptVariants.title: Price concern
promptVariants.openingLine: I understand what your product does, but I'm not sure the price makes sense for us.
promptVariants.userGoal: Acknowledge the price concern, ask one discovery question and connect value to business impact.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Do not defend the price immediately. First learn what the problem currently costs them.

promptVariants.title: Timing concern
promptVariants.openingLine: This looks interesting, but I don't think this is the right time for us.
promptVariants.userGoal: Explore the timing concern and identify whether there is a smaller next step.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Ask what would need to change for this to become a priority, then suggest a low-pressure next action.

promptVariants.title: Existing tool
promptVariants.openingLine: We already use another tool for this, so I'm not sure we need to change anything.
promptVariants.userGoal: Respect the current setup, ask what is working and uncover one gap or improvement area.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Do not attack their current tool. Compare outcomes, workflow friction or missed opportunities.

suggestedPhrases: Could you tell me more about...
What would the impact be if...
It sounds like the main concern is...
followUpPrompts: Before we talk about price, what question would you ask to understand the customer's real concern?
How would you connect the product value back to the customer's own words?

feedback.summary: You acknowledged the concern well. Ask one more discovery question before defending the product.
improvements: Ask about current cost of the problem
Tie value to the customer's words
feedback.suggestedRewrite: That makes sense. Before we talk about price, could you tell me what this problem currently costs your team in time or missed opportunities?

roleplays.title: Workplace Small Talk
roleplays.description: Practice short workplace conversations before meetings or with new colleagues.
roleplays.workplaceContext: You are joining a call a few minutes early with a colleague you do not know well.
roleplays.userGoal: Start a natural conversation and keep it professional.
roleplays.openingLine: Hi, I don't think we've met before. How's your day going?
suggestedPhrases: How long have you been working on this project?
followUpPrompts: What friendly follow-up question would you ask to keep the conversation natural?
How would you politely move from small talk into the meeting topic?

feedback.summary: The conversation sounds friendly and appropriate. Add one follow-up question to keep it moving.
improvements: Use the person's name if you know it
feedback.suggestedRewrite: Nice to meet you. My day is going well, thanks. How long have you been working with this team?
